summary: Gherardo Gnoli (1937–2012) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies scholar who studied at Sapienza University of Rome. He taught at Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993) and Sapienza (1993–2008), and served as president of ISMEO (~1979–1995).

Ghulam Yazdani (1885–1962), a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, graduated from Aligarh Muslim University (B.A. 1905) under Mohammad Ishaq and Nazir Ahmad. He held professorships at St. Stephen's, Rajshahi, and Lahore before directing Hyderabad's Archaeological Department (~1914–1943).

Giacomella Orofino is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1977–1981) and Sapienza University of Rome (1982–1985) under Raniero Gnoli, and later taught at Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2000–2007).
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda (1888–1953) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (-1914). He served at Kyoto University as lecturer (1929) and assistant professor (1934–1948), and later held professorships at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.
Giho Okada (1882–1961) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito (1909–1996) specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, linguistic, and Indological studies. Educated at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki, he held posts there including professor (1968–1972) and later served as professor at Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

Gil Fronsdal (born 1954) is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Stanford University (attested 1998), studying under teachers including Jan Nattier and Carl Bielefeldt, and was affiliated with the Sati Center and Insight Meditation Center.
Gilbert Kenneth Jenkins (1918–2005) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Bloxham School, he served at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

Gilles Tarabout works in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Madeleine Biardeau. As of 2004, his positions included senior fellow at CNRS, member of EHESS, and exchange program director at the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme.

Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2008) under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin, also studying under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.

Giovanni Gentile (1875–1944) was a philosopher educated at Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and the University of Pisa. He held professorships at Palermo (1906–1914), Pisa (1914–1917), and Sapienza University of Rome (1917–1944), and founded ISMEO in 1933.

Giovanni Vacca (1872–1953) was a scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at the universities of Genoa and Florence. He taught at the University of Florence (1910) and held appointments at Sapienza University of Rome from 1911 to 1948.

Giovanni Verardi (born 1947) works in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied at Allahabad, Banaras Hindu, and Gorakhpur universities. His career includes posts at Ca' Foscari (1972–1987), Bologna (1981–1987), and a professorship at Naples "L'Orientale" (1988–1993).

Girindrasekhar Bose (1887–1953) was an Indian scholar of psychology and philosophy. He studied at Presidency University, Medical College Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta, where he served as Professor of Experimental Psychology (1917–1949). He also founded the Indian Psychoanalytic Society.

Gisela Emma Full is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the universities of Würzburg and Münster. In 2013, she held research fellow positions at European University Viadrina and the Samueli Institute.

Gisho Nakano (1891–1977) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and at Kyushu University. He held professorships at Peking University and Koyasan University, serving as president of Koyasan University (1951, 1964).
Giuliana Martini is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at the Italian School of East Asian Studies and Kyoto University in 2010.

Giuseppe Bardelli (1815–1865) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien, and served as a lecturer in Coptic and Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (~1845–1848).

Giuseppe Caspar Mezzofanti (1774–1849) was a linguist who studied at the University of Bologna (~1789–1797). He served there as professor of Hebrew and later Oriental languages (~1814–1831), and became Custodian-in-Chief at the Vatican Library in 1833.
